atoms.name: Node, head, next
atoms.one_line: Each node holds data and a pointer to the next node. The head pointer is the only entry.

atoms.name: Insert and delete at the head
atoms.one_line: Constant time: rewire head. Anywhere else needs a pointer to the neighbour.

atoms.name: Singly versus doubly linked
atoms.one_line: Deleting a given node is O(n) in a singly list (need predecessor), O(1) in a doubly list.

atoms.name: In-place reversal
atoms.one_line: Three pointers: prev, cur, next. Θ(n) time, O(1) space.

atoms.name: Tracing pointer code
atoms.one_line: Draw boxes and arrows. Update arrows in program order. Watch NULL and uninitialised next.

atoms.name: Circular lists
atoms.one_line: Last node points to the first. A rear pointer reaches both ends.

atoms.name: Slow and fast pointers
atoms.one_line: Fast moves 2, slow moves 1. Finds the middle and cycles.

atoms.name: Recursion on lists
atoms.one_line: Base case at NULL or the last node, then recurse on next.

atoms.name: Sorted lists, merge and meld
atoms.one_line: Sorted insert is Θ(n) each. Merging two sorted lists takes Θ(m+n).

atoms.name: Python Node class
atoms.one_line: Node objects with .next. Names are references, so aliasing applies.
